descriptionChirho: The act of overstepping or violating a divine command or law; a willful breach of God's established boundaries. Used in Paul's theological arguments about the relationship between law and sin (Rom 2:23; 4:15; 5:14; Gal 3:19; 1 Tim 2:14; Heb 2:2; 9:15). Multilingual evidence is semantically unified: Spanish 'transgresión/transgresiones', Hindi 'अपराध/अपराधों' (offense), Arabic 'مُخالَفَة/التَّعَدِّيَات' (violation/transgressions), Korean '범함/범죄들' (committing crime), Swahili 'uvunjaji/makosa' (breaking/faults). The singular (S73794) and plural (S73795) forms express the same concept of legal-moral transgression in different grammatical numbers.
